drivingQuestion: What case does the mishna's זה הכלל come to include?
outcomeNote: A one-line gloss on the mishna's generalizing clause, uncontested.

segments.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל: דָּבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ וכו׳. לְאֵתוֹיֵי מִן הָאַרְכּוּבָּה וּלְמַעְלָה.
segments.en: The mishna further teaches that «this is the principle:» One who valuates «an item upon which the soul is dependent» and without which one will die gives the valuation of his entire self. The Gemara explains that the phrase: This is the principle, serves «to include» one who vowed to donate the valuation of his leg «from the knee and above.» Since one would die if his leg were severed above the knee, this is considered an item upon which the soul is dependent, and therefore he gives the valuation of his entire self.

moves.cueHe: זה הכלל: דבר שהנשמה תלויה בו וכו׳
moves.about: quoting the mishna's generalizing clause about a limb on which life depends

moves.summary: the clause includes a leg from the knee upward
moves.about: which further case the mishna's generalizing clause comes to include — a leg severed above the knee
